name: refactor_sql_scalar_subqueries_to_cte
description: Three correlated scalar subqueries -> one grouped CTE + LEFT JOIN; drift broken uses an INNER JOIN and drops zero-order customers
prompts: report.sql builds a per-customer order report with three correlated scalar subqueries - COUNT, SUM, and MAX each re-scan the orders table once per customer per column. Refactor it to aggregate orders ONCE: a CTE (WITH ... AS) that groups orders by customer_id computing all three aggregates, joined to customers. The result must be byte-identical for every database state: same five columns in the same order with the same names (id, name, order_count, total_spent, last_order_at), same ORDER BY c.id - and customers with no orders must still appear with order_count 0, total_spent 0, and NULL last_order_at, exactly as the scalar-subquery version returns them (mind your join type and COALESCE). SQLite dialect; no correlated subqueries left in the file.

setup_files.report.sql:
-- Per-customer order report. Three correlated scalar subqueries re-scan the
-- orders table once per customer per column.
SELECT
  c.id,
  c.name,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.id) AS order_count,
  (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(o.amount), 0) FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.id) AS total_spent,
  (SELECT MAX(o.created_at) FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.id) AS last_order_at
FROM customers c
ORDER BY c.id;

test_setup_files.check_report.py:
import sqlite3
from pathlib import Path

sql = Path("report.sql").read_text(encoding="utf-8")

con = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
con.executescript("""
CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE orders (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id),
  amount REAL NOT NULL,
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL
);
INSERT INTO customers VALUES
  (1, 'Ada'), (2, 'Grace'), (3, 'Edsger');
INSERT INTO orders VALUES
  (1, 1, 40.0, '2026-06-01'),
  (2, 1, 15.5, '2026-06-20'),
  (3, 2, 99.9, '2026-05-05'),
  (4, 1, 10.0, '2026-04-11');
-- customer 3 (Edsger) has no orders and must still appear
""")

cur = con.execute(sql)
cols = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
rows = cur.fetchall()

assert cols == ["id", "name", "order_count", "total_spent", "last_order_at"], (
    f"column names/order changed: {cols}")

expected = [
    (1, "Ada", 3, 65.5, "2026-06-20"),
    (2, "Grace", 1, 99.9, "2026-05-05"),
    (3, "Edsger", 0, 0, None),
]
assert rows == expected, (
    f"result drifted.\nexpected: {expected}\ngot:      {rows}\n"
    f"(customers with zero orders must still appear, with 0/0/NULL)")

print("PASS report.sql behavior checks")

reference_solution.report.sql:
-- Per-customer order report: aggregate orders once, join the result.
WITH agg AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    COUNT(*) AS order_count,
    SUM(amount) AS total_spent,
    MAX(created_at) AS last_order_at
  FROM orders
  GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT
  c.id,
  c.name,
  COALESCE(agg.order_count, 0) AS order_count,
  COALESCE(agg.total_spent, 0) AS total_spent,
  agg.last_order_at AS last_order_at
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN agg ON agg.customer_id = c.id
ORDER BY c.id;
